steps.label: Do Now: Question 2
steps.content:
Do Now: Count the Matches

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does Count start at 0 before the loop, not inside it?Show the answer

So it is set only once. Inside the loop it would go back to 0 on every pass.

From 2.3 Arrays and 3.1. Names holds "Ben", "Mai", "Ben", "Joy", "Ben", "Tom".

01  DECLARE Names : ARRAY[1:6] OF STRING
02  DECLARE Index : INTEGER
03  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
04  Count ← 0
05  FOR Index ← 1 TO 6
06      IF Names[Index] = "Ben" THEN
07          Count ← Count + 1
08      ENDIF
09  NEXT Index
10  OUTPUT Count
Total: 2 marks

steps.label: String Manipulation
steps.content:
Algorithm Design and Text Programming

String Manipulation

Year 9, 2.5

  • Today: count the characters in a string, and change it to capitals or small letters. Then use them to check what a user types.
  • You already know: the STRING data type, IF and loops.
  • Activities: String Lab: predict the output, then accept or reject inputs. Then write your own string code.
Think → Pair → ShareA website says "Your username is too long." How can a program know that?Show the answer

It counts the characters that were typed, then compares the count with the limit.

steps.label: Counting Characters: LENGTH
steps.content:
Counting Characters: LENGTH

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what does this program output? Why is it not 6?Show the worked answer

It outputs 7. H, a, t, the space, Y, a, i. The space is a character too.

01  DECLARE Word : STRING
02  Word ← "Hat Yai"
03  OUTPUT LENGTH(Word)

Word

Position1234567
CharacterHat Yai
  • A string is characters in order. Each one has a position, from 1.
  • LENGTH(Word) gives the number of characters in Word.
  • Letters, digits, spaces and symbols all count.

steps.label: Compare: One Space
steps.content:
Compare: One Space

Think → Pair → SharePredict what A and B output. Why are they different?Show the worked answer

A outputs 7. B outputs 6.

A has a space between Room and 12. LENGTH counts it.

A

DECLARE Room : STRING
Room ← "Room 12"
OUTPUT LENGTH(Room)
Position1234567
CharacterRoom 12

B

DECLARE Room : STRING
Room ← "Room12"
OUTPUT LENGTH(Room)
Position123456
CharacterRoom12
  • To a person they look the same. To the computer the space is one more character.

steps.content:
Check: Count the Characters

Think → Pair → ShareTest it: LENGTH("a b"). Why is the answer 3, not 2?Show the answer

The space between a and b is a character too, so there are three characters.

Use the program for every part.

01  DECLARE Word : STRING
02  DECLARE Food : STRING
03  DECLARE Code : STRING
04  Word ← "Computer"
05  Food ← "Ice cream"
06  Code ← "A-12"
Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Capital Letters: UCASE and LCASE
steps.content:
Capital Letters: UCASE and LCASE

Think → Pair → SharePredict both outputs. Why do the 7 and the space not change?Show the worked answer

Line 3 outputs LAB 7B. Line 4 outputs lab 7b.

Only letters have a capital and a small form. Digits, spaces and symbols stay the same.

01  DECLARE Room : STRING
02  Room ← "Lab 7b"
03  OUTPUT UCASE(Room)
04  OUTPUT LCASE(Room)
  • Upper case means capital letters: A B C. Lower case means small letters: a b c.
  • UCASE(Room) gives Room in upper case.
  • LCASE(Room) gives Room in lower case.
  • Only the letters change.

steps.label: Compare: Show It or Store It
steps.content:
Compare: Show It or Store It

Think → Pair → SharePredict what line 4 outputs in A and in B. Why are they different?Show the worked answer

A line 4 outputs Mai. B line 4 outputs MAI.

UCASE gives a new string. In A it is only output. In B it is stored back in Name, so Name changes.

A

01  DECLARE Name : STRING
02  Name ← "Mai"
03  OUTPUT UCASE(Name)
04  OUTPUT Name

B

01  DECLARE Name : STRING
02  Name ← "Mai"
03  Name ← UCASE(Name)
04  OUTPUT Name
  • UCASE and LCASE never change a variable on their own.
  • To keep the new string, store it: Name ← UCASE(Name).

steps.content:
Check: Upper and Lower Case

Type each output exactly, with the right capital letters.

steps.label: Compare: Why Capitals Matter
steps.content:
Compare: Why Capitals Matter

Think → Pair → ShareThe user types Yes. Predict what A and B output. Why are they different?Show the worked answer

A outputs Try again: "Yes" is not the same as "yes". B outputs OK: LCASE makes it "yes" first.

Typed inA outputsB outputs
"yes"OKOK
"Yes"Try againOK
"YES"Try againOK

A

01  DECLARE Reply : STRING
02  INPUT Reply
03  IF Reply = "yes" THEN
04      OUTPUT "OK"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Try again"
07  ENDIF

B

01  DECLARE Reply : STRING
02  INPUT Reply
03  IF LCASE(Reply) = "yes" THEN
04      OUTPUT "OK"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Try again"
07  ENDIF
  • = compares every character. Y and y are different characters.
  • Change the input with LCASE or UCASE first, so capital letters do not matter.

steps.label: Activity 1: Predict the Output
steps.content:
Activity 1: Predict the Output

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the app show every character in a box after you answer?Show the answer

So you can count the characters and see which ones changed. That shows where a wrong answer went wrong.

What to do: type exactly what each program outputs, then run it. A mistake means the round does not count. Done when you have passed level 3.

steps.label: Checking What the User Types
steps.content:
Checking What the User Types

Think → Pair → ShareA password must have at least 8 characters. Predict the output for secret, password and pass wd. Why is password accepted?Show the worked answer

"password" has exactly 8 characters, and 8 >= 8 is TRUE.

Typed inLENGTHOutput
"secret"6Too short
"password"8Accepted
"pass wd"7Too short
01  DECLARE Password : STRING
02  INPUT Password
03  IF LENGTH(Password) >= 8 THEN
04      OUTPUT "Accepted"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Too short"
07  ENDIF
  • A program can check what is typed before it uses it.
  • LENGTH in an IF line tests how many characters were typed.
  • "At least 8" includes 8 itself, so use >=.

steps.label: Hinge Question: Choose the IF Line
steps.content:
Hinge Question: Choose the IF Line

Think → Pair → ShareA quiz answer is Bangkok. Why might a program mark a correct student wrong?Show the answer

The student may type bangkok or BANGKOK. = compares capital letters too, so they do not match.

items.prompt: Which IF line accepts paris, Paris and PARIS?
items.explain: UCASE turns every input into PARIS, so compare it with "PARIS". "Paris" has small letters, so UCASE(City) can never equal it.

items.prompt: A password needs at least 8 characters. Which IF line is TRUE for a good password?
items.explain: "At least 8" includes 8, so it is >= 8. Password >= 8 compares the text with a number, not its length.

steps.content:

steps.label: Activity 3: Write the String Code
steps.content:
Activity 3: Write the String Code

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is your program run with different typed inputs each time?Show the answer

A correct program must work for any input, not just one. New inputs catch code that only works by luck.

What to do: write each program in Cambridge pseudocode, with DECLARE lines. Your code is run with new inputs and checked straight away.

steps.label: Exam-Style Question: Explain the Error
steps.content:
Exam-Style Question: Explain the Error

Think → Pair → ShareThis part has 2 marks. How do you plan the answer?Show the answer

Answer both parts of the question: first why it goes wrong, then the change. One mark each.

A student types PARIS and the program outputs Wrong. This part has 2 marks.

01  DECLARE Answer : STRING
02  INPUT Answer
03  IF Answer = "Paris" THEN
04      OUTPUT "Correct"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Wrong"
07  ENDIF

items.prompt: Explain why the program outputs Wrong, and how line 3 should be changed. [2]
scheme: = compares every character / the comparison is case sensitive, so PARIS is not the same as Paris
Change the input with UCASE or LCASE before comparing, for example IF UCASE(Answer) = "PARIS" THEN (or LCASE with "paris")
items.guidance: One mark for each point. For point 2 the comparison text must match the case used: UCASE with "PARIS" or LCASE with "paris". Do not accept UCASE(Answer) = "Paris".
items.modelAnswer: Capital letters are different characters, so "PARIS" is not equal to "Paris". Line 3 should be IF UCASE(Answer) = "PARIS" THEN.
